newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus exchange inches upwards after lows.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus exchange inches upwards after lows.

text.p: Cyprus's stocks tumbled 2.14 percent during the week as political tension between Cyprus and Turkey earlier this month caught up with the bourse.
Cyprus's exchange fell to a low of 77.45 on Wednesday, losing 1.16 percent in one day but managed to reverse the trend in the last two days of the week, where shares made gains of 0.65 percent.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) all-share index, set at 100 points, closed on Friday at 77.96.

"The low business and investment morale is fed daily with conflicting views on the prospects of the economy," said CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation in its weekly report. Other analysts have also expressed fears that the tension could affect tourism, a principle source of revenue for the island.
Banking stocks closed at 87.58, down 2.40 percent from last week's close. Shares of the Bank of Cyprus retreated 11 cents to close at 324.5. Popular Bank POPB.BY shares closed at 318, down 7 cents.
Hellenic Bank HBCP.CY shares gained three cents, closing at 262, while the Universal Savings Bank gained half a cent, closing at 138.
Approved Investment stocks closed at 69.41, down 3.91 percent in the week. Insurance corporations closed at 55.95, marginally lower than 56.05 recorded last week.
Universal Life insurance made gains of 15.5 cents to close at 388. Paneuropean Insurance were trading at 112.5, down two cents from last week. Interamerican lost 4 cents, closing at 97.5.

Cement producer Vassiliko closed down 4 cents to 149, while the Cyprus Cement Company closed at 230, down 3.5 cents from last week. Beer and wine producer Keo closed the day at 108, down 2.5 cents in the week.
